newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends sharply higher on stocks.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends sharply higher on stocks.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed sharply higher, and traders said nearby December gained on short-covering tied to tight deliverable stocks of wheat, traders said.
"We had...a short-covering flurry," an MGE trader said. "I think there was some flour pricing early and that got things started and we just keep going higher."

MGE spring wheat closed two to 16-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 16-1/2 cents at $4.17. March gained 11-1/2 cents to $3.91-1/2. The last time MGE Dec spring wheat closed above $4.17 was October 15, when it ended at $4.17-3/4.
Traders said the surge came amid fears of a squeeze in deliverable wheat stocks. Friday, November 29, is first notice date for deliveries on MGE spring wheat.
Wednesday's short-covering allowed the Dec/March inversion to widen and close at 25-1/2 cents after trading early at 20 cents.
"It's tightness in the cash market and the fact that nobody wants to be short the front month right now," an MGE trader said earlier in the session.

Traders said Benson-Quinn bought 1.2 million March and 900,000 Dec bushels. BQ also bull-spread 500,000 Dec/March bushels. LFG and Atwood/Peavey each sold at least 800,000 March. Atwood/Peavey bear-spread 1.8 million March/Dec and Wilson bear-spread one million March/Dec at 22 to 23 cents.
MGE barley futures closed five to 10 cents per cwt higher, with Dec not trading. March gained 10 cents to close at $6.60.
The MGE estimated Wednesday's spring wheat futures volume at 25.6 million bushels, up from 20.7 million Tuesday.
